t: Use a ship cannon to shoot down demons attacking the ship.

We're getting closer to the wormhole. We had a pretty hard time, the ship is barely holding itself together... What the hell?!
...
Demons! Demons attacking again! Fire in the hole! All hands on deck!!
May they get devoured by the Astral, we'll have to jump into an unknown sector blindly, unprepared! May the Light save our souls!
Why are you just standing there? Grab a cannon and show those astral shrimps how things are done in Siveria! We just need to get through to the wormhole, and then we're in the clear!
How do you feel? Dizzy? Do you see multi-colored spots?
Praised be the Light, you're OK!
With Marianne de Ardeur's help, go to the Purgatory and talk to the Servant of the Light.

Defeating Nihaz, the God of Darkness, didn't make us any happier. I'm afraid we only pushed the world closer to its downfall. I'm not gifted with clairvoyance, but I have a feeling we're missing something very important. Something... evil. And not only me!
The servant from the Purgatory spoke to me a while ago. Can you imagine?! Given his self-righteousness and lust for profit, this stingy goblin needs something extraordinary to happen for him to condescend to mere mortals! And it does seem to have happened.
The servant told me about some strange Sparks stuck in the Purgatory. The Sparks of some poor bastards can't return to their bodies or leave the Purgatory. They don't vanish either but wander idly among the heroes waiting for their turn to be resurrected... That's horrible!
Please go to the Purgatory and find out what has befallen those Sparks. You don't even have to die to do that - simply talk to me, and I'll help your Spark leave your body.

Hey! Wanna jump the line?!
Wait a sec... I remember you! You're that hero who helped the goblins and the ghosts on Gipat! You were sent by Marianne, right? Nice girl, yep!
Inspect the lost Sparks in the Purgatory and find out what happened to them. Report to the Servant of the Light.

Oh, something's rotten in your kingdom, yep! Look at those poor souls restlessly wandering through the Purgatory. Empty eyes, empty heads... It's horrible!
I don't know what happened to them. They appeared in the Purgatory already like this, with neither will nor power. I tried to talk to them, but to no avail, yep. They talk nonsense. I saw crazy Sparks before, and all of them would leave this sorrowful place after a certain time... But not these, they wander around here, scaring the dead, and cannot return, as if they are stuck between life and death. Perhaps you can try to talk to them? It is not good that our set routines be interrupted by some lost souls, yep.
First they pass to and fro, then honest folks are losing Sparks!
So that's how it is! Cultists, then... I think it's time to warn Marianne!

Tep's cultists did it! Oh, what in the world blew me to the Frozen Peak!... First the astral pirates riddled my ship, so it finally broke to pieces above that wicked place... We thought it a miracle that we were nearly landing and everybody was safe...
Then those cultists appeared out of nowhere! They pinioned us and dragged us somewhere... My clothes were all torn! I finally found myself in a large crate... That's all that I remember...
Damn it! If only I could gain my strength to break away from here, I'll kill those bastards!
Find traces of a shipwreck at the Frozen Peak.

So it's the cultists... I've never met them myself - those fools don't believe in the Light. However, they have complete trust in every word of their prophet Tep, may his bald skull be eaten through by herpes! You, however, must have already come across them in battle. So it's you who's going to handle this mess!
I'll bring you back to the world of the living. Go to the Frozen Peak and find the spot where that poor bastard met his death. Try finding out what exactly happened to him and why his Spark is in such a sad state.
Now go. And try not to visit me too often, eh? Good luck!
The snow is trampled down around the wreckage. There are some traces of blood. There must have been a serious battle here!
Get inside the pyramid and find the prisoners.

The traces are hard to see, but that's enough to understand that a vicious battle took place here! The sailors and mercenaries stood their ground against the cultists, but they were clearly outnumbered. Interestingly, there are no dead bodies or weapons around.
Looks like the cultists didn't want to kill the Kanians who survived the shipwreck but rather capture them. In which case, they might be alive! Or just one of them, at least...
The cultists' tracks lead towards Tep's Pyramid that looms on the mountain. The prisoners must have been taken there!
Kill 10 Tep's Cultists and their prelate Sarbaz Dhoru, take Tep's orders off his body and deliver them to Aidenus in Novograd.

Goddamned cultists... They fell on us like snow trolls, immobilized us all by spells. The bastards even killed the senior aide! Those who were conscious were tied up and brought to the pyramid. They didn't torture or beat us; in fact, they ignored us completely. They stuffed everyone into this hole and began to take one after another away. I don't know exactly where to.
The cultists are led by some evil prelate. Sarbaz Dhoru is his name. A real mean bastard! After I asked what they wanted from us, that walking corpse punched me so hard that my teeth became loose. I wish I could find the prick and tear him apart, but I'm too weak to handle the dirtbag. But I'm sure you can take care of him. He and the other cultists must not go unpunished! Find the bastard and kill him. He had some papers on him that can hopefully help you find out what those bastards want and where they took the rest of my friends. When you're through, hurry to see Aidenus! He must know what happened to our guys.

Tep's cultists? Again?! Oh, a thousand astral demons! That insane sorcerer is the last thing we need...
You're not the first to bring such sad news. A while ago, the cultists attacked our settlements in Darkwater and Siveria and even raided the military camp on the Coba Plateau! A few knights got killed! Voisvet starts gnashing his teeth every time he receives the mirra bill for our army.
What's that? Cultists' documents? Give 'em to me!
Well, well... Let's try finding out what those fanatics want.
Find Tep Cultists near the Brazen Hill, exterminate them and rescue the captives, then bring the good news back to Aidenus.

The documents you secured make me think that we underestimated the threat those wackos pose to the whole world. Tep ordered his servants to kidnap all the rational beings they can and take them to some place hidden deep in the Astral. We were unspeakably lucky - the captured papers contain the coordinates of the cultists' den!
I will immediately order our combat squadron to get ready for take-off. It's time we stamped out that cultist plague once and for all! As for you, I have another order that's less heroic but equally important.
After we raided the military camp by the Brazen Hill, we were missing a few rookies. I thought they were dead and waited for resurrection in the Purgatory, but upon reading these documents, I'm afraid they were captured by Tep's servants. I'm sure the cultists didn't make it too far. Please go to the Coba Plateau, find our guys and rescue them! I'm scared to imagine what the damned fanatics can do to them if we don't hurry...
Hurry up! I'm scared for the ordinary people captured by the fanatics...
The captives are saved? Oh... That's a relief! On behalf of the entire Kania, I thank you for saving their lives!
Find Tep Cultists near the Valir Settlement, kill them and rescue the captives, then bring the good news back to Aidenus.

The Brazen Hill is not the only place where our warriors recently encountered cultists. Just now, I got news of cultists raiding the Valir Settlement in Darkwater. They slashed the guards to pieces and took some of our subjects away with them. I'm afraid we'll never see them again if we don't hurry up.
Go to the Valir Settlement, find those damned cultists and annihilate them! Their rotten breath must not defile the Kanian air! But most importantly, rescue the captives! Their lives are in your hands, hero!
Hurry up! I'm scared for the ordinary people captured by the fanatics...
The cultists couldn't finish what they started and their bodies are lying around in mud? Well, that's well deserved!
Find Tep Cultists near Gravestein, kill them and rescue the captives, then bring the good news back to Aidenus.

The damned cultists managed to get as far as Siveria! They caused a snowstorm and stealthily attacked the residents of Gravestein. The settlement residents fought bravely and threw the enemies back, but some of those slain have not risen yet. Now I understand they were captured, and I'm asking you to go there, find the cultists and rescue the captives!
Don't delay! There's no time to waste...
The captives are saved and the cultists received their just deserts? Great news! I knew you wouldn't fail!
Question the workers at the port, find the traitor and bring the proof of treason to Aidenus.

You managed to save a few lives while I... I sent an entire squadron to a certain death! We shouldn't have trusted the Empire! Never ever!
Tep is not only a threat to the League, or the Empire, or old fools like myself. No, he brings death to all living beings! And I was so naive as to decide we could only take care of him by siding with the Empire! What a blunder of mine...
I sided with Yasker himself. The Empire's soldiers faced the cult's intrigues. He had nothing left to do but agree on joint actions against our common enemy. But was it a common enemy?
Two squadrons, ours and the Empire's, went to the known coordinates, and then the comms with our ships were down. We lost our best squadron! Now our capital is exposed to attacks by the enemy fleet. Izbor suspects treason, and I'm inclined to agree with him. Seizing the opportunity to deliver a treacherous stab in our back is typical of the Empire. This only means one thing - we have a rat in our midst! Find it!
The squadron's deployment was top secret, only the workers and the port guards knew about it. Question them all, find the traitor and make him talk!
The Empire's saboteurs are extremely well-prepared, but remember - even the best spies have their cover blown by trifles...

What? The traitor was one of the guards? And she had an encrypted message on her? Strange and suspicious. The answer is too simple, the decision is too stupid, the suspect is dead, but she confessed everything before she died... And Committee agents are not especially talkative, you know!
We'll try deciphering the message, but only Tensess knows how much time it's going to take. I don't know who's behind it all, but we seem to be playing by someone else's rules...
Meet with Gleb Puskarev, captain of the Stiletto.

Despite any doubts, I believe we must take action. If you don't know what to do, do anything!
To find the missing squadron, I sent Stiletto, a new ship that's fresh off the shipyard, on a search mission! That brig is speeding through the Astral faster than a thought, and its long-range weapons can shoot even an Octulhu full of neat holes. The ship is under command of a proven captain named Gleb Puskarev. But I want someone on board whom I can trust like myself. Someone capable of handling any problem... I mean you!
The ship has a teleport beacon installed on it, so one nod is enough for your Adventurer's Stone to drop you directly on Stiletto's deck. And may the Light be with you!
Thank the Light, you are fine!
Ask Nukah Scraggy-Bone to show you the way to the pangolin's lair, defeat it and brag about your victory to Cheebah One-Eye in the Glittering Wing settlement.

I heard that you're a great wingless hunter. I know where to find a prey worthy of a legend! A terrible pangolin! Its roar makes trees tremble and its step makes earth quake. It is a real beast!
If you want to prove your valor, you should hunt the beast. Nukah Scraggy-Bone knows where beast's den is and he'll show you the way. If you kill the beast, I'll give you a nice reward!
Bigger animal, more glory for hunter!
Good catch! Outlander be mighty hunter to fell such beast. You get good reward!
Use the long-range communicator to establish communications with Novograd and report the situation to Aidenus.

How can we get in touch with Novogard, eh? We have no Adventurer's Stones, and teleport spells aren't working. Even the elven master who was on board of the flagship only shrugs his wings and mutters something queer about distortions in astral channels and displacement of some kind of nodes. I guess we're stuck deep here... Oh, whatever will we do? We may have to utilize that secret elven invention. I just hope it doesn't break down...
Here, take it. This thing is called a long-range communicator. It was made by elves! If they're telling the truth, we can use it to get in touch with any sorcerer in Sarnaut. However, it's only charged enough to last two minutes.
Well then, let's try contacting Aidenus.

Damm...t... Comm...s Nee... Adju... Freq...cy... Wai... sec...
...
There! Finally I was able to get through the distortions. Looks like something hinders me from tuning in to you.
Is this the much-praised elven long-range comms? Hm... Nice, but not too practical.

What's up with you? Why didn't you contact us? Why didn't you report the situation? You received no further instructions but rushed headlong into an unexplored sector?
What? Speak up! I can't hear you!
Dammit...
Find the ruins of an ancient June portal on the coast, try awakening them with your Adventurer's Stone and report the results to Clement de Ardeur.

Oh, the comms are down... Whatever will we do? Think, my dear brain, think...
Bingo! I got an idea! Clement, a scientist from House de Ardeur, mentioned something about stone ruins not far from the camp. He said they looked like a portal and have been there since the June era. However, it was non-functional when we checked it. We'd kick and rub it, and the elf would cast all kinds of spells - it just wouldn't work. But we didn't have an Adventurer's Stone, which you do! All Stones are linked to portals, we know that for sure. What if your Stone can awaken the portal?
Trying costs nothing, after all. Go see Clement and try doing something about that goddamned portal. What exactly? How should I know?! Bang your head against it or strike it with your Stone!
Get creative! Actually, that's not a bad idea. No, not the one about the head! I'm talking about the Stone. Perhaps contacting the magic slumbering inside the ruins can awaken them, eh? That would be great!
Goddamned portal... I've never felt so absolutely helpless!

How?! How did you manage it?!
I've been racking my brains trying to awaken those ruins, but nothing would come out of it... And now, they nearly came back to life! Though I wouldn't risk binding a Stone to them. You can easily miss while being teleported and end up being fused into the allod's center...
Use the long-range communicator to establish communications with Novograd and report the situation to Aidenus.

That's interesting... If I have the slightest idea of astral science, we're now in the middle of nowhere! The coordinates of this place don't seem to exist at all! I think if you try using the Stone to go to Novograd now, you're unlikely to get back here. Yeah, we're stuck all right. You can't even call a rescue mission with teleportation experts.
But there's some good news. The remains of June magic can allow us to establish reliable communications with Novograd. Try calling Aidenus again right now!
Finally, I can hear you too! Come on, tell me what's going on and why you didn't get in touch for so long.

I'll be damned... The entire squadron perished in a blink of an eye... Shame on my gray head! I had a gut feeling we shouldn't have made that temporary alliance with the Empire. Now, we'll have to use all our forces to protect Kania against a potential attack. How inopportune... But anyway, it's not the time to complain. We must take action.
Because you have an Adventurer's Stone, you'll have to be a messenger between me and the survivors. Listen up.
No one in this world knows about the allod you found yourselves on. I checked all astral maps made since the discovery of astral flights, but I found nothing. So you'll have to act at your own peril.
I'm sure Tep did everything to make his secret refuge inescapable for intruders. Although the fleet is destroyed, any information about Tep can end up being extremely important to us. So keep searching!
Your having an Adventurer's Stone on you is sheer luck, but it can help us all. The Demon Hunters' destroyer is now barraging the area around the entrance to the wormhole, exterminating nearby demons. The Hunters don't interfere with politics between the League and the Empire, but the threat Tep poses concerns us all, so they agreed to help. They have a teleportation expert and a portal device on their ship. If you can't come to your enigmatic allod directly, I'll bind your Stone to the portal on the Hunters' ship. Teleport there right now and try getting into the wormhole once again. If it exits directly above the allod, the worst thing that can happen is that you simply black out again. Then go back to the admirals and report my instructions.
Where have you been? We ran off our feet looking for you!

What? Aidenus orders us to adapt to circumstances and continue looking for Tep here? I'll be damned! With no comms, supplies or support... That's madness! But if we don't do it, who will? So we'll make it!
Meet with Karrok Stout-Hearted, the leader of the Glittering Wing tribe, and tell him about the tribal sign found on the Deadman's Rock.

Oh, I'm not sure at all! What if I falsely accuse the whites of allying with the Empire? They seem to value their words more than gold. Birds of honor, they are. If we make such a blunder, they won't even talk to us after that. Indeed, diplomacy isn't easy. Negotiating from a position of force was always more to my liking. You pull a sword, put it to the other party's throat and hand them your protest note. If your political opponent refuses to accept your note, you take a good swing and lay an embargo straight between their eyes. Oh, those were good times...
But never mind. Here's what I think. The aviak ruler owes you his life. Show him this emblem. If these birds really are plotting something, they won't touch you. A life for a life, that's how it works. And if they're not to blame, let them help us find the culprit, for it's in their best interest!
Quarr, friend. Why do you disturb me? I have already told you what I think about that piece of evidence. For now, I have nothing to tell you.

Where did you get that sign?! That's the sign of our sworn enemies, damned red traitors. They call themselves Steel Claw tribe! Long time ago, we were one tribe. But there were fools who wanted equal rights. A lady and a nest for everyone, and no need to work! They wanted a stupid thing, a revolution. There was the war, an old town was burned down. Now, there are two settlements, two tribes and a never-ending war.
Tell me why did you go to their settlement! You could not get the sign of Steel Claw anywhere else.
Meet Elchana Speak-with-Spirits on Kahlua Island.

Did you find the sign in the camp? And were there evil outlanders calling themselves Empire? Bad news for all of us.
I trust you - our scouts noticed a strange human watching our town. They spotted red-winged one next to him. Your sign reinforces my concern. If red-winged ones ally with the Empire, we'll be in trouble. They will summon their stupid Council and ruin everything our ancestors created. That cannot happen!
I, Karrok Stout-Hearted, speak on behalf of Glittering Wing. Our people and wingless outlanders need to make an alliance. Our future can be secure by solid authority, and that is our strength!
But we cannot enter into treaty without blessing of elements. Wind that carry us, earth that give us shelter, sea that feed us, and fire that burn in our dwellings all are our patrons. Only Elchana Speak-with-Spirits understands them. She lives on Kahlua Island, to the east of our town. You, Son of the Wind, should go ask Elchana to talk to spirits. I've spoken my word, let them speak theirs.

Ah, wingless outlander did come see me. Let me guess... Karrok send you! He wants our spirits to bless the alliance with outlanders that came from the great void? All right... You shall hear their word!

Listen and memorize. Each element has its own power. When you touch an element, it shares its power with you. Water heals your wounds, fire boosts your energy, air makes you very, very fast, and earth gives you reliable protection. Ask...
What's going on?! I sense presence of a strange spirit, but cannot see it. Help...

I see it in your eyes that you expected another kind of talk with the old man? Well, sorry. I warned you that your actions incurred the wrath of mighty enemies. Luckily for you, those are my enemies too.

To defeat one of the minions of Sihal, the master of this giant illusion... Once again, I was right in assessing your abilities. Without my help, though, you're going to be stone-cold dead very soon.
Remember I promised to show you how deep the rabbit hole was? I guess you'll have a few minutes to get ready for the journey while I'm opening the entrance. A way back is not foreseen, sorry - it's a one-way ticket.
Pass all trials given by Sea Master and meet Earth Master on the Ashy Wasteland.

You can now better understand the circle of life that is never interrupted. Hot blood, wild and incoercible, pumps through your veins like water in a mountain stream. You justly deserve my blessing! Still I wish to test you, and this is mostly for your sake.
If you pass the trial, turn your steps toward a place called the Ashy Wasteland, where you will be met by my brother, the master of everything that grows. He is named the Cliff Master, and his temper is as severe as a sharp cliff. He will show you the way further...
Humm... Who dares to interrupt my sleep?
Mortal. Pathetic. Weak. Frail. Wants to understand the power of earth? Hear the rumble of rocks? Humm... Well, let them try...
Collect starfish from the sea bottom and bring them to Sea Master on the Isle of Singing Water.

My blessing is expensive. I want to entrust a trial to you. First a simple one, then one a bit harder.
A sky full of stars... Did you ever stop to think where they come from? Did you ever make a wish at the sight of a star that broke loose from the firmament in a swift flourish? As years go by, however, the stars do not disappear... Why do you think that is? Get me a handful of stars from the sea bottom, and I will tell you that secret.
The sky is but a reflection of the water surface...

Yes, mortal... The stars that fall from the sky get straight into the ocean, their splendor splashing. These drops give birth to starfish that will, in time, shine in the sky, thus ending the cycle of their lives like you ended the first trial...
Exterminate 12 Venomous Cnidaria and report your success to Sea Master on the Isle of Singing Water.

Water can be different: tender and affectionate, quiet and serene, icy and gloomy, roaring and fierce... Equally different creatures dwell in the depths of the sea. I am joyful about each, I cherish thoughts about each, I look after each. Just as a gardener roots out the weeds in a green meadow, I cleanse the clear water from filth as best I can. If you want to grasp the essence of water, you will help me in my laborious endeavor.
The sea is full of life, but there are those who, though endowed with life, only bring death to others. I am speaking about stingers whose venom can turn an elixir of life into that of death. Will you be strong enough to take care of that plague? If your answer is "yes," you will have my blessing.
All living beings are worthy of living, but what procures its life through others' deaths is worthy of nothing but dying...
I can hear words of gratitude in the swashing of water. Those words are being said by all sea creatures, both small and big. You have passed my trial with valor!
Gather some Jellyfish Slime from Venomous Cnidaria and Snake Venom from Horned Vipers and bring them to Sea Master on the Isle of Singing Water.

I have the toughest trial for you. Many brave warriors met their death trying to complete this laborious task. However, those who fear danger shall not have my blessing. Now listen to my will and perform it exactly that way!

There are lots of venomous reptiles in the world, and each of them has a purpose, a place in the circle of life, each makes way for another life with that of its own. There are those, however, driven by death alone who strive to spoil the vortex of life with their venom. Death-Adder is its name, and there's nothing better for it than turning life into death. However, that serpent is extremely cunning and only able to attack on the sly. Your task is to lure it. And to make a bait for the venomous reptile, you will need another type of venom. Although it is not so strong, its filthy stench is to that reptile like heavenly fragrance...
I weed out the field in pain, protecting myself against a greater pain...
Here it is, the filthy liquid that brings death to all living beings. However, just like death is followed by life, this venom will be used to the benefit of life, too.
Lure Death-Adder with the smell of the venomous mix spilled on the southern coast of the Isle of Singing Water, kill it and tell Sea Master about your feat.

From a mix of venoms, I will make one that can even turn rocks into sand. Its smell is not dangerous, albeit rather filthy, so only a reptile that has even more venom will be drawn by it. Death-Adder is strong and its venomous fangs have killed a lot of worthy beings. The water that washes its filthy form will never bring about new life, but its death will be a boon.
Spill a drop of the venomous mix onto the stones. Lured by the smell, Death-Adder will appear before you like death incarnate. Don't be afraid, defeat the reptile in combat. New life will be brought about by its death, and you will have my blessing that very instant!
Life emerges from the water, breathes air, gets warmed by heat, goes into the earth and returns into the water. This is the eternal cycle that should not be broken.

The fluids of underground waters told me about the black blood spilled onto the sand. Let it be... What emerged from the water, should turn into water once more. You have passed your trial brilliantly!
Find the shipwreck survivors on the Rainbow Atoll.

It looks like this is the wreckage of neither the League, nor the Imperial ships. Look at the strange color of the ship camouflage. And the wood is rotten... I wonder who could have sail on this to Irdrich. Maybe we should search for the survivors.
Equip the weapon in your bag. Then talk to Quartermaster Birchy the Merciless.

Listen up, everyone! We've got every single private accounted for! Equip yourself, on the double! Unless you think that the League soldiers will simply surrender the moment they spot your bare hands!
You! What are you waiting for? Scared, are ya? Is this your first battle, rookie?
Well, if you don't want it to be your last, you better move it! Obey, and you just might make it out of here in one piece!
Hey, equip your new weapon! You know I'm not just the quartermaster... I'm also in charge of handing out punishments to anyone who's disobedient on this ship!
That's it! Now get in there. You're one of the last shreds of hope for the survival of this ship.
Equip the weapon in your bag. Then talk to Quartermaster Birchy the Merciless.

Listen up, everyone!
We've got every single private accounted for! Equip yourself, on the double! Unless you think that the League soldiers will simply surrender the moment they spot your bare hands!
You! What are you waiting for? Scared, are ya? Is this your first battle, rookie? Well, if you don't want it to be your last, you better move it!
Obey, and you just might make it out of here in one piece!
Hey, equip your new weapon! You know I'm not just the quartermaster... I'm also in charge of handing out punishments to anyone who's disobedient on this ship!
There! Now you're nearly invulnerable! The hope and support of the whole Empire, I say!
Use the Battle Cocktail and then talk to Birchy the Merciless.

You look great! Our uniform suits everyone - Xadaganians, Arisen, Orcs... Now for my favorite task... don't worry, you'll be fine. You've not done anything to deserve it so far. But if you act like a coward, if you abandon a comrade on the field of battle, or if you break any of our rules, then you can be sure I'll be coming after you!
Take this. It's a battle cocktail, a potent little shot of invigorating, revitalizing, liquid courage which turns pansies into true warriors. Drink away, don't worry, it's allowed in the rules. Come on soldier, don't mess around!
What's with the face? Sure, maybe it doesn't taste like fruit juice but its benefits are amazing.

Can you feel it working? Has it kicked in yet? It's sure to get you going. Heck, it might even have you feeling like you can take on the entire League Army! It's the latest invention from the Imperial scientists, it's been known to transform even the most cowardly of goblins into real warriors.
Defeat the League troops and return to Whir the Unyielding.

Seems like I poured you a stiff one just in time. The battle is about to begin! So, whatcha waiting for? Attack! You gotta fight off the League's assault troops before that battle cocktail wears off!
Go straight for the enemy's leader! They won't put up much of a fight without him. Onwards, for the Empire! For our homeland! For Yasker! For Nezeb!
Give them everything you've got! What are you waiting for, you pansy?

Well, it seems like I can't call you a pansy any more. You've won your first battle! I got this armor from the ship's stash to help gear out the recruits. For doing such a good job I'll give you first pick. Go ahead and choose what you like the most.
Defeat 4 League Troopers and 1 League Veteran and talk to Sarang Minx.

I have a new task for you, rookie. League assault troops have captured the armory! This is unacceptable! Go there right now and slaughter every one you see! We must remove the bastards from our ship.
When you're there be on the lookout for a scientist named Sarang Minx. He was in there when the League attacked and he might still be alive, although it's not likely. The League assault forces are ruthless executioners, and they take mercy on no one!

Thank you for the assistance... Huh... What's wrong with my legs? They're not moving. It appears that my arteries are shot and my mechanisms are severely damaged... How much blood and oil have I lost? Looks like more than I should have...
Take the Activation Key from the safe and bring it to Yasskul Odzhi.

Listen up carefully... The assault party was targeting this safe here. It's storing an activation key for a very important item, but unfortunately I can't tell you more since this is highly classified information.
The key's security has obviously been compromised, so you must open the safe and take the key to First Mate Yasskul Odzhi. He'll know what to do with it. Tell Yasskul that the League assault was not a random act... the League knows all about... the "device". I can't explain any more, but he'll understand.
What's the matter, soldier? Don't tell me there's more bad news.

Sarang Minx believes this was no ordinary attack? Hm... This changes things. We should review our tactics. I'll need to consult with the Captain.
Thank you for giving me this news. As for the activation key... Well, you seem to have a good head on your shoulders. And most League troops would never suspect that an ordinary soldier like you is carrying something important.
Keep it with you for now, but remember that it is the property of the Empire and must be returned to me as soon as this fight is over!
Hit the League ship using the Cannon and return to Yasskul Odzhi.

Hold it! At my command!
One of our bombardiers has gone down from enemy fire. Man the free cannon and fire at the League ship with everything you've got! We need to blast them to pieces!
What are you doing talking to me for? Did you take out that ship yet?

What beginner's luck! You hit the League ship's power line and took it right out. It'll be a while before they recover from this! Good job! I salvaged this from one of our wounded crew mates. Take it!
Talk to Sarang Khafre and determine the cause of power failure.

Damnit! The League assault troops hit us hard and disabled a large part of the ship. We had to turn on our secondary power generators, but for some reason they're starting to fail too!
I need you to head to the reactor room on the double! Find Sarang Khafre and see what's going on. And if this is the result of another of his stupid experiments... tell him I'm going to rip his hardware out!
We're in a tough spot. We can't get rid of that shield and our power is fading!

What? Of course I had nothing to do with this! What do you take me for, an idiot?! Open your eyes rookie!
League assault troops captured the reactor room and are wreaking havoc in there!
Use the Neutralizer to destroy the magical shield, kill the Fire Elementals, and talk to Sarang Khafre.

See?! They're destroying the reactor, and without it we're doomed! Some blasted Kanian cleric created a shield that's blocking our access to it, too.
Do you see those fire elementals? Those damn Kanians probably summoned them there. It's only a matter of time before they completely obliterate the device!
We have to destroy the shield! Take this neutralizer and help the other technicians remove the cleric's shield. After you destroy the shield, kill those fire elementals at once!
Those fire elementals make it pretty hot in here...

Perfect, the reactor is back under our control! Here, take one of my weapons, I'll be too busy trying to fix the reactor anyway. Oh no... the captain is going to kill me! One of the League assault troops stole something very valuable from us!
Tell Kazimir Sablin that the device has been stolen.

Circumstances are forcing me to violate my security protocol. I am about to tell you extremely classified information.
A Kanian crusader stole something from us... let's call it a device. It is an equipment of high security and value to the Empire. Now that I think about it, I'm sure this whole attack was designed to steal our te... mm... device.
Go see the captain and tell him about this new complication. We need to send an assault team to the Kanian ship! Otherwise Termitka Prison will be our new and only home...
Get back in there and get the reactor back under our control!
Son of a... I told Sarang Khafre a million times to let me keep that device! But no, he had to go and experiment with it!
Make your way onto the Kanian ship, use the Activation Key, and defeat Gradimir Kozlov.

Assault team? We have two cannon crews down, an entire team fixing the reactor, and the rest of the men fighting those League bastards on deck. I'm not sending an assault team, I'm sending you!
You see, the device he stole was a personal teleporter that was supposed to teleport our soldiers out from the midst of battle. Why didn't it actually work and save our men? Because it's a piece of crap! Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't... and most times it doesn't.
Fortunately they didn't get the activation key. Grubin tells me you're actually the one who kept it safe! That means they won't be able to actually use the thing themselves, but that's the only complete prototype in the Empire right now so we need to get it back!
Go up to the outer deck and use the landing pad to get to the League ship. Once on board, use the activation key to attune the personal teleporter to yourself. That should interfere with any of their attempts to use the device. Then defeat the crusader and get it back!
If you're lucky, you might actually make it through this in one piece. If not, I'll make sure to personally nominate you for a service medal. Posthumously, of course, and that's if I manage to get out of this mess myself.
How are you feeling? Looks like you are getting better.
I'm glad you are doing fine. Everyone was talking about the hero who alone managed to destroy a League ship.
Equip the weapon that Svetobor Ratnev gave you and report to him for further orders.

This is a tragedy! We must take matters into our own hands and notify League officials about the assassination of Clement de Desirae. Our only chance for survival is through a portal located on the first floor of the tower. We need to head to the portal immediately!
Consider this a field promotion, your service in the League's Army has officially begun!
It would have been nice to be better prepared for the situation, but unfortunately we cannot afford that luxury. Here, take this weapon, it'll have to do.
Kill 3 Laboratory Rats and talk to Svetobor Ratnev.

Through this path lies Clement's laboratory... Hm, Clement's lab rats appear to be blocking our path. The Great Mage Clement used to put them through all kinds of odd experiments, so now the rats are extremely vicious.
The assailant must've broken the cages and released them while they were retreating. We must kill all the lab rats if we're to make it through. Let's move!
Impressive. You're more reliable than you look.

I found a piece of old armor in the laboratory. Take it. During times of war you must use whatever resources you can to your advantage. You must always remember one thing... Wait, hold on! Someone's alive in the corridor!
Talk to Boris Hopelesaev in Clement's Tower.
It's Boris Hopelesaev, one of the elite members of the League Defenders! Attend to him immediately and I'll talk to the others.

Treason! It was Kirill Meshersky, the Chief of the Guards... It was he who led the rebels into the tower! They caught us by surprise, we stood no chance against their assault... many... dead. My wound is too deep. I don't have much time left, but please tell me everything.
Kill the young manticore, find out the fate of Lev Hopelesaev, and report your findings to Boris Hopelesaev.

The Great Mage is dead?! How?! If that is indeed true, this allod will soon crumble! Listen... in the next room are even more of Clement de Desirae's experiments. A few guards were sent down here to contain them when the tower began to crumble, but Meshersky released the violent manticore.
Among the guards was my brother Leshko... my younger brother... he was in that room to help contain the beast. If you find my brother Lev please bring him to the portal... Lev has to be there... it's hard to imagine that the unthinkable has already happened.
Go into that damned zoo and kill the manticore - I know you can do it! Please find out what has become of my brother, I must know that he's safe!

...Oh Great Light, abandon me not with your mercy, grant me redemption and just retribution...
Ah, it's you... Where's Leshko?
Dead!? I... at least now I know that I'll be joining my brother soon. That damned Kirill! I've never trusted those nobles! They need to be dealt with before it's too late!
Check on Svetobor Ratnev in Clement's Tower.

You must survive... the Astral will swallow the tower soon... It's coming. Everything... will be destroyed... You need to head down the stairs to find the portal, it's the only way to escape...
You should check in with Svetobor and see if he is okay... the heavy shaking in the tower just a few moments ago... I heard something collapse down the corridor... I hope that nothing bad has happened...
There's no one to support this allod... everything will be destroyed.
Slay the Kanian traitors and Kirill Meshersky and speak to Glok the Knife.

Rookie, this is my final order! Survive! Do you hear me?! Survive, whatever it takes! You must reach Kania and tell the League officials what has happened here.
Access to the stairwell is blocked, you'll have to jump down below. Be careful though, the rebels are stuck in the same room.
Avenge us... the Hopelesaev brothers, Clement, all those who have died in this travesty.
Go... I will remain with Boris. We served many years together in the League Army, perhaps we shall appear before the Holy Tensess together as well.

You were wonderful out there! Rookie huh? Didn't look like one to me. Please tell me what's happening out there. One moment I'm helping prepare for the banquet, and the next moment everyone's fighting.
One thing's clear - we need to teleport off this allod! Unfortunately, the rebels are fighting us near the base of the tower, and they won't let us anywhere near the portal.
Find and use the Elixir of Invulnerability and return to Glok the Knife.

What a fight that was! Hey, you're wounded! You didn't even notice huh? If my brothers Lok and Shpok were here, we would've protected you! One Gibberling is good enough, but three can stand toe-to-toe with even the strongest of Orcs.
We need to patch this wound immediately! Normally I'd recommend a bandage but since we're in Clement's office... let's see...
I know, check out that chest over there! I saw him keep useful potions and elixirs in that chest. Once he mixed three components together, poured it over a wound, and it magically healed right before my eyes. You need to find one of those elixirs!
Have you found the elixir yet?

How was that? You feel pretty good, don't you? It's definitely quite the elixir considering that it instantly healed your wounds. I'm sure Clement must have been saving it for a special occasion. I found some useful items around the room while you were gone. Please choose one that fits you the best.
Find Amanda de Desirae in Clement's Tower.

Listen, I'm going to go on ahead of you. There are still lots of people outside that need to be brought in. I'm also worried about my brothers. You know, we Gibberlings are sore to be alone.
You should go down and make your way through to the floor below us. Clement's niece Amanda should be in there. The two of us had been fighting off the traitors together, but she came up with some sort of plan that involved magic. Please find her and make sure she's safe, okay?
I'll be off then. Good luck!

I heard about my uncle's death... My uncle was not only my mentor but a great man who had lived through the Great Cataclysm.
It's unforgivable that he fell by the hand of Kanian conspirators! Unfortunately, now is not the time for remorse - we must activate the portal and evacuate this tower.
Defeat the Magic Elementals and talk to Amanda de Desirae.

See this magic device right here? It's nearly a thousand years old. My uncle was an avid collector and he kept this Resistance Sphere in working condition.
This very device was used by Great Mages of the past to keep allods from being devoured by the Astral. Of course, there have been great advances in the field of magic since then and no one has used these antiques in ages, but this sphere may still prove itself useful.
I'm not a Great Mage, but I will try my hardest to activate it. There is no other choice, we must activate the Resistance Sphere to buy us more time to make an escape portal.
I must warn you though, using the Resistance Sphere has a potentially negative side effect. It's possible that elementals will appear because their power is tied to the Resistance Sphere itself. They do not want us draining away their energy source. I'll focus on activating the sphere, just support me if anything happens!
Thanks for your support! I'm surprised that the elementals actually appeared.

I wasn't able to complete the ritual but I bought us enough time to at least make it to the portal room.
I've been carrying these weapons around with me and I don't have much use for them. I need to focus on activating the portal, you know. Why don't you take one?
Escort Amanda to the portal downstairs and talk to Shpok the Knife.
Let's hurry to the portal! I'm sure Glok is already downstairs waiting for us with his brothers.
There you are! Praise Tensess for bringing you here safely!

Did you see the undead?! That's the handiwork of the demonologist's below.
It wouldn't shock me to find out that the Great Mage's blood is on his hands. Who else could've summoned up a Shadow that terrible?
Slay Raimond de Doucer and talk to Amanda de Desirae.

Who told me about the shadow? Glok, of course. When he returned, we attacked those Kanian rebels together and nearly took them all out! All of them except that awful demonologist. He raised those who had fallen and now there are dozens of zombies on his side.
It's a strange sight, an Elf and Kanian rebels working together.
We're up here while my brothers, Lok and Glok, are outside gathering the rest of the people. The demonologist and his undead are downstairs and they're the only things standing between us and the escape portal.
We need to go downstairs and kill the undead and that douchey Elf. When they're out of the way, we'll activate that portal and get outta here.
When Glok told me about your valiant duel with Kirill Meshersky, I didn't believe it at first. But now that I've seen you with my own eyes, I know he was telling the truth!
Before you go take this. I found it on the demonologist and I'm sure he won't be using it anymore. Now let's get out of here!
Hold off the Astral demons while everyone evacuates the Tower, then talk to Amanda de Desirae.
I'm going to make sure that door stays open and everyone gets in. Amanda will focus on activating the portal. I have a feeling some more trouble might be coming our way, so keep your eyes open!
Amazing work! You gave us just enough time to open the portal and evacuate most of the people in this tower.
Use the portal to escape the doomed allod.

Soon the Astral will swallow up this miserable allod. We should head through the portal ourselves now. Soon we will be safe and sound in Novograd!
Here, take this. It's a magical Meteorite Stone that I found in my uncle's lab. According to his notes they're used to stabilize the portal to make sure we make it through in one piece!
Well, off we go. And may Tensess watch over us!

Hi there! I am Selene de Ardeur, the famous poet! How lucky you are to be stranded with someone like me. I'm sure you just adore my new poem, right? "Love is a magic country, where the spring rules..." You haven't heard it? Hm...
What do I mean by stranded? Well, look around. After we took the portal in Clement's Tower, we all thought that we'd appear in Novograd. But fate is a crafty feloness! We appear to have ended up on a deserted allod instead.
Amanda said that these strange Meteorite Stones that she gave us would make sure we got to the right place. But as you can see, she wasn't quite right. Poor thing, she is so upset right now!
Listen to Nihaz's speech until the end.

Welcome to the Dead City, my trusty helper! Are you still trying to understand all the secrets of the world? That's quite commendable! I already told you that brawn does not decide everything. It's not enough to just be strong. You have to know how to apply this strength. So it is that this is the position you are in. The throne room of the Dead City is where everything began, and it's where everything will end... All of the figures in our story are already in their places and are squirming with anticipation, so eager are they to play their roles in our new play. Three acts simultaneously on three stages! And you will be playing the lead role. For my part, I'll stay here in the audience.

Look right. The first stage is behind those gates - the foul demon ruins. I'm sure they're just dying to break free and tear everyone in the audience to shreds! It's too bad they're too weak to tussle with a god. No matter what they do, their powers are essentially useless, because the gates open on my command!
Right behind me you can see the entrance to the second stage, lit only by the crimson flame of the scaly horde of draconids and their Fiery Father. They tried to outplay me on my own turf. And they failed. They just don't know it yet, haha.
Last of all, behind the third set of gates are waiting some of the once-great Junes, now resembling the worst of a drunkard's nightmare: wormfaces, led by their relentless leader, Zakom. It was his Spark that they were able to steal from me on the Isle of Revelation. He's got a new body now... But something tells me that it's not a perfect fit.

The best part is that all of them - the draconids, the wormfaces, and Sarn's demons - all fear something more than me! They are afraid that someone else will get here first, to the heart of the Dead City. Each of them is trying to reach an agreement with me behind the others' backs, promising to help destroy what they imagine are my enemies, their own mates. Hah! Can you imagine, they all want to settle their scores with their long-time enemies by having someone else do the dirty work!
You can probably guess what brought them all, wormfaces, draconids, and even the demons here to the Dead City? Hehe. Look up! See that huge construction? That is the key and the lock in one. But let's leave its purpose a secret for now. It will be made clear to you when the time comes. It's not good to change horses midstream, right?
Let the presentation begin!
Participate in the murder of Lickflame Tinderbox in the Upper City, then report to Nihaz.

Oh, the efforts of my enemies - and yours, too - are truly entertaining. To think that anyone hopes to challenge me on my own terms and on my own turf and actually win... You can't make this stuff up! For instance, Sarn's demons really want Lickflame Tinderbox to die. That draconid was one of their Fiery Father's first sentient creations. The demons hate him almost as much as they hate the Great Dragon. The Great Dragons were Sarn's jailkeepers for many thousands of years... They still haven't totally worn out their welcome with their idiocy and inability to accomplish the simplest tasks.
But we'll talk of the Great Dragon some other time. As for Lickflame, that overgrown scaly freak... In contrast to his creator he can use the powers of my Seals, and Sarn and his henchmen understand that if the draconids are able to make their way here to the throne room, Sarn will always remain a prisoner. The Demons are even willing to help me if it means being rid of Lickflame. Imagine that! Demons! Willing to help! Me! Haha!
But you don't look a gift horse in the mouth, isn't that right? You should know that if you decide to get rid of Lickflame (which will have to happen sooner or later), then the demons will happily help you with that.
Oh, how I love these moments... My enemies are destroying one another!
He won't ever walk again? Excellent...
Defeat the three Trainers and tell Nihaz of your victory.

The dragons hate the wormfaces with all their souls. I may be their enemy for the moment, but the wormfaces are their eternal sworn enemies. After all, the wormfaces were once the Junes. I created the dragons, and the Junes exterminated almost all of them. The Great Dragon has no real reason to hate me, and he has many reasons to wish for the wormfaces' destruction. He especially thirsts for the blood of Shilonen, Coatl, and Atslan. One of them was once a great sage and philosopher. The second was a powerful wizard, and the third - a shrewd warrior. But their skills helped them not in the battle with the cursed Sarn. So they came crawling to me on their knees and became what you see now.
So why do the draconids want them to die? Hah! The wormfaces's knowledge remained as June as ever, regardless of their appearance. And this trio is capable of teaching the others how to deal with the dragons. If they haven't already... It matters not. What does matter is that if you wish to fight them, the dragons might well become your temporary allies.
I wonder why the number ‘three' figures so heavily in the myths and legends of this universe. Not two, not four, not seven, but exactly three... Strange.

One, two, three... Oh no, the wormfaces have lost their trainers and sages. What rotten luck!
But it's nice to watch your enemies gnashing their teeth at the base of the mountain when you're sitting pretty on top. Look, friend. See what stupidity leads to. Instead of putting their efforts into setting and achieving goals, my enemies spend all their energy on pointless horseplay. Choose your goals and your enemies wisely, sweet thing, for only then can you achieve power, glory, and respect.
Participate in the destruction of Nav and report to Nihaz upon completion.

The curse of Junes... No, they're not so much a "curse"... Rather, they are aborted astral primordial matter and pawns in the hands of Sarn. Although they did almost wipe the Junes out completely. You know, it's quite fascinating to watch your enemy, who was once afraid to dirty his neat little clothes with even the slightest bloodstain of sacrifice, now set the whole world awash in gore?
Let the Junes hate me all they want, but being transformed into wormfaces was clearly not without benefit. Finding themselves in a clumsy, puny body, they began to use their brains instead of their brawn. They were even able to surprise me, by stealing my discovery, the Spark of the last June. And the best part is that they put his Spark into a wormface body!
Now Zak, reborn, thirsts for revenge. Not against me, which you'd have expected, but rather against the demons, because of whom his people were annihilated. So if you decide to create a little brouhaha and exterminate the demons, the wormfaces will probably help you in this noble undertaking.
Strangely the situation turns sometimes, yes? Enemy, friend - who can tell who's who?
A demon more, a demon less... On the global scale, the destruction of one of the astral spawn will have no effect except to add more spice to the show that's unraveling before us.
Participate in the murder of Ath-Zak and report of your success to Nihaz.

It's time to end one of the plotlines in our show. Zak is a pain in the butt, frankly speaking. Capricious and ignorant. And yet you all consider him to be some sort of a hero? So he defeated a demon, barely and with the help of a Great Mage. Big whoop. Ugh!
Either way, the fools that snatched his Spark consider him almost a divine figure. They follow him like a herd of sheep. Once was not enough for them, apparently. We'll have to review the lesson.
Pass through the gate to the Lower City and put an end that annoying Zak once and for all. As a Spark he's much more tolerable.
Zak's still not the chatty type, eh?

That means I won't be listening to his idle babble for the coming centuries. Thankfully. Ha ha!
Perhaps I'll even move his Spark to a new body after a while... After all, his people almost defeated the dragons, and he alone had enough pride and courage to stand against me. Which means there's hope for him, yet.
Participate in the murder of the Earth Destroyer and report to Nihaz upon completion.

Well then, time to deal with Sarn's demons. Our prisoner's starting to get a little restless. Who knows, he might actually be able to break out his prison. If that happens, I won't be able to rebuild; I'd just have to smite him. But he's more useful to me in one piece. It's fascinating to watch how with every effort to free himself he acquires a new stain of darkness on his offensively pure soul. He'll never get those stains out, haha!
Here in the Dead City, demons obey the Earth Destroyer - a self-propelled battering ram capable of "destroying the walls of a jail cell," thus freeing its creator. Joking aside, this time Sarn created almost the ideal administrator for his plans, a helper intended for two tasks only: death and destruction. More and more, Sarn reminds me of me when I was young! I too was always looking to create all kinds of different monsters before I learned that brute force always loses out to careful calculation.
But brute force just might do the trick in this situation. So, my friend, I need you to hunt down the Earth Destroyer. It's a powerful foe, to be sure, but if you can put together a good team you'll defeat him without any trouble.
We're destroying the universe, tearing it down to its foundation... I've heard these slogans before!
Has the Earth Destroyer been killed? Excellent. I appreciate that. Let my godling friend sit in limbo and think about what he's done, eh? Haha!
Participate in the destruction of the Great Dragon and report back to Nihaz.

Know what I hate more than anything? Stupid, petty treachery.
Take, for example, the Great Dragon. I forgave him for failing to guard the prison. Everyone makes mistakes. But his attempt to go to war against me resembles a stray pup trying to pick a fight with a mature wolf dog - pointless, petty, and stupid. Seems he has forgotten who he's dealing with! I'll have to remind him.
Go with a troop to the Upper City and rid me of this overgrown lizard. He's no longer interesting to me.
Fools! Their plotting is so primitive that even a child could figure it out! What are they counting on?

Is the dragon destroyed? Hehe. I wonder how the horde of draconids will get on without their Fiery Father? Although, there's still Soliskar the Wise and Agrus the Callous... No big deal. They're not interfering now. I hope that they can learn their lesson well and not try to cross me. And if they should once again start meddling where they don't belong... What's one more dead dragon, right?

Finally... You have no idea what tortures I endured in that body! Cursed Nihaz... It's all his fault. His lies brought my people to a disgraceful end.
I... I don't even have the words to curse him! And you... I don't hate you. You are but a blind pawn in the dark god's game. I even feel thankful that you've freed me from my agonies. In thanks, I'll tell you the real reason that compelled me to challenge Nihaz.
Long ago, when my people were strong, we were almost successful in wiping out the dragons. But Nihaz appeared and said that if Sarn were to be freed, the universe would be destroyed, and us with it. My ancestors grew frightened, though I believe that it would have been better had they all perished... But Nihaz can be convincing. He showed us the Star Gates, a structure that the gods use to move between worlds. He promised that if there was any danger he would give us a new world in which we would reign. And when Sarn's curse wiped out almost all of my people, the survivors ran to Nihaz, tearfully beseeching him to fulfill his promise and take them to a new world, where the curse would have no effect.
What's interesting is that Nihaz almost never tells a direct lie. And he wasn't lying in this case, either. We were given a new world. A world of damp, subterranean caves and eternal darkness. The curse stopped following those who were no longer Junes. But it would have been better if he had lied and simply destroyed the survivors... Death is better than this fate.
Do you see that this will be your fate, too? Nihaz speaks the truth, but his words are pure poison, for truth can have many faces. And you always hear the truth that you want to hear. It's not too late to come to your senses! Challenge Nihaz and take him down. Otherwise, sooner or later his lies will destroy you, more surely than the keenest blade!
Hahaha! The puppy has teeth? Well I'll be...

Ungrateful scum! ME! I raised you above the herd of sheep! I gave you strength! I gave you knowledge that exists nowhere else in the universe! And this is your thanks?
Better you'd have heeded the old saying about the hand that feeds you!

You only just draw nearer to the slowly dissolving, floating figure of the defeated demon, when you are overcome with a flood of visions.
You see Sarn vainly struggling to destroy the darkness that binds his body, radiating a pure white glow. Every jerk elicits a painful grimace in the god of light, and his body remains stained by the shadow of darkness. The stains grow with each attempt to escape.
You can see that Nihaz has played his own game with the imprisoned god, a cruel experiment where every attempt at freedom brings Sarn closer to his breaking point, where he will have no more strength to battle darkness and will become just like Nihaz. The god of darkness has entertained himself for years, offering Sarn the chance to escape from his prison, but then repeatedly dashing his hopes at the last minute.
You see a strange structure installed in the throne room of the Dead City, and you can see that it is the Star Gates, Sarn's last hope. If the demons could take the gates, then Sarn would be freed and could leave this world. But foul Nihaz once more forges his victory on the labour of others, the labour of the heroes of this universe who believed in his good intentions.
History repeats itself... Once, the Junes believed Nihaz and were destroyed. The same fate awaits both the League and the Empire. The only chance to escape the tragic lot of the Junes is to stop Nihaz before it's too late.
You... You have the audacity to raise your hand against a god?
Traitor... I had hoped that at least someone in this universe was able to appreciate the beauty of my ideas. I raised you above the rest... And this is your gratitude?!

A mortal... I have been defeated by a mortal... Unfathomable! Me, the Greatest of the universe's first Keepers, brought down by a miserable worm tunnelling in the dust at my feet!
You must be proud of your victory... Go ahead, be proud. Your master will leave you in the dust just as he left us in our day.
When Nihaz imprisoned Sarn and locked him up within Sarnaut it was us, the twelve Great Dragons, that were to guard his prison. We performed our duty admirably! But Sarn is a god, and we, the keepers, as potent as we are, are not omnipotent. The prisoner found a way out and created life on a planet, giving it a mind of its own and then turning it upon us. I'm talking about the Junes.
By the time we realized that we would not get by on our own, it was too late. We called upon our Master, and he responded... But he turned away from us with a mocking laugh! Nihaz strengthened the walls of the prison, locking them with the twelve Seals, and he turned us out to die at the hands of pitiful creations! But I survived. I found a way to escape that world and became truly free! Gathering my own army of draconids, I waited for Nihaz to return. Dragons are nothing if not patient...
During the Cataclysm some of the Seals were damaged, and the astral merged with the Seals' power, flooding the world and ripping it to shreds. Nihaz did not hasten to intervene, but I waited patiently, and it paid off!
Along with Nihaz in the Dead City appeared the Star Gates, the source of divine power! With their help, one can travel through the worlds, drawing energy from each new world, acquiring knowledge and power. I wanted to capture the gates while the Master was occupied with the world's problems. I'd have used it to create a new world for myself and my children. If it hadn't been for you, I'd have succeeded...
Nihaz is deceiving you, have no doubt of that. Your only chance is to strike first!

That winged worm put you up to this? To betray your own daddy? Not good... You really think that a god can be killed with ordinary weapons? Hahaha!
You were able to destroy my corporeal body, this husk. Too bad my little girl isn't around... No matter.
Presently I may not in the condition to turn you to ash on the spot, but remember, vermin, I will return. And if I happen to be in a good mood, I'll give you one more chance to serve me. Better you agree, if it comes to that, or else the tortures that my friend Sarn endured will pale in miserable comparison!
Go to Yasker and tell him about the secret of the Patrons.

Remember, fool, only the gods or forces equal to gods can destroy gods. And you, parasites, are abusing this force! "Patrons"... what a joke. Yet another lie is all it is. Couldn't you at least lie with dignity...
There were no Patrons. Or, more to the point, all of your mages croaked in the Cataclysm. Croaked, and that was that. And the floods that you and yours use so brazenly - I created those! First I gave some of my power to the dragons, but those brainless lizards wasted it left and right, weakening all the while. The power left them like wine through a sieve. Predictably, they were left weak and vulnerable... Of which the Junes took advantage, mowing them down almost to the last. Then I traded in the dolt dragons for Seals: concentrated power meant for a single purpose - keeping Sarn imprisoned. If it hadn't been for your Cataclysm, the whole thing might have lasted for quite a while. Luckily for Sarn and unluckily for us, catastrophe befell the Seals, and part of their power was lost to the astral. Part of my power!
The dragon's power, the remnants of which were utilized by your mages, and the power of the Seals, which you are using now while calling it Patronage - all of this power came from me! Do you really think that you can destroy me with my own weapons?
Frankly, I'm not even offended by your actions. Moreover, I would have thought less of your bravery and ambition if you hadn't challenged me. But I must say you picked the wrong time to interfere. You still can't use the Gates, no matter how hard you try. Tell your Yasker that I said he can go get bent! As for you, we'll see each other again!
I see you are itching to tell me something? Judging by your tight lips and crazy eyes the news is not going to be good, eh?

Hrm. I wasn't mistaken. It's not good news. But it seems to me you did the right thing.
The Star Gates... Can you imagine what would have happened if the Empire had taken them? More than likely, we would have succumbed to temptation and set off to conquer new worlds. The Empire would have swelled to monstrous proportions, massive power and prestige. And then? I'm tempted by these lovely visions, but I know all too well what unfettered expansion brings. Believe me, I have experience, and it's a tragic story.
Now, about the Patrons. Do not ever tell anyone what you know. Yes. There were no great martyrs. But this is one of the biggest government secrets, one of many that you know that must not be revealed. The people needed a symbol to rally around, and we gave them such a symbol. Twelve symbols, to be exact. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. You can tell the Keeper of Secrets everything that you know, but don't divulge where you got your information!
Go to Aidenus and tell him about the secret of the Patrons.

Remember, fool, only the gods or forces equal to gods can destroy gods. And you, parasites, are abusing this force! "Patrons"... what a joke. Yet another lie is all it is. Couldn't you at least lie with dignity...
There were no Patrons. Or, more to the point, all of your mages croaked in the Cataclysm. Croaked, and that was that. And the floods that you and yours use so brazenly - I created those! First I gave some of my power to the dragons, but those brainless lizards wasted it left and right, weakening all the while. The power left them like wine through a sieve. Predictably, they were left weak and vulnerable... Of which the Junes took advantage, mowing them down almost to the last. Then I traded the dolt dragons in for Seals: concentrated power meant for a single purpose - keeping Sarn imprisoned. If it hadn't been for your Cataclysm, the whole thing might have lasted for quite a while. Luckily for Sarn and unluckily for us, catastrophe befell the Seals, and part of their power was lost to the astral. Part of my power!
The dragon's power, the remnants of which were utilized by your mages, and the power of the Seals, which you are using now while calling it Patronage - all of this power came from me! Do you really think that you can destroy me with my own weapons?
Frankly, I'm not even offended by your actions. Moreover, I would have thought less of your bravery and ambition if you hadn't challenged me. But I must say you picked the wrong time to interfere. You still can't use the Gates, no matter how hard you try. Tell your Aidenus that I said he can go get bent! As for you, we'll see each other again!
Well, well, what brings you and those burning eyes of yours to my office?

I see... Not the best news imaginable, that's for sure. Listen to what I have to say. After the catastrophe, simple folks needed a symbol to unite around, and that's what we gave them. Well, twelve symbols, to be exact. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. And the power... Who cares whose power it is, as long as it's being used for good? Power is neutral. We, the sentient beings, are the ones who give it its bias.
To be honest, it's nice to have my hunches borne out. For now, it's not important which ones.
As for the Star Gates, I'm actually pleased to know that they are inaccessible to us. Imagine what would have happened with them at our disposal? The Gibberlings would have found themselves a new land. The elves' great houses would have sprung up everywhere, only to quickly wither for want of competition, and the pursuit of beauty in innovation. As for the Kanians, they'd have lost their roots, forgotten their ancestors and their faith... And what is a people without roots? Dust on the roads of history! It will be better if you don't tell everyone what you've learned...
Show Nihaz the dead man's seal in the throne room of the Dead City.
This seal belonged to the long-dead ruler of the Dead City. Maybe we should show it to Nihaz!
The dead man's seal? Interesting. Perhaps I can resurrect the fallen ruler if we collect the rest of the relics and bones.

Gather the relics of the last king of the Dead City and bring them to Nihaz.

Here in the throne room of the Dead City, I sense the presence of something I cannot see...
It's a ghost! The last ruler of the Dead City, as far as I can tell. What does he want?
...
Oh, so that's it! He was not slain in honest battle, as befits a king, but rather fell at the hand of a hired killer. A familiar story... Now he wants another, peaceful death. For this to happen, he requests that we remove the relics that belonged to him in life. They can be found on the undead in the Dead City. We will then resurrect him long enough to slay him in a proper battle.
Shall we help this long-gone king, or should we leave him to haunt the ruins?
If you want to bring the dead king to life, bring me his crown, his blade, and his seal. Oh, and about twenty of his bones, too.
Aha! Get ready to fight! Something tells me that the ghost wants to rest, surrounded by his fallen enemies, as would befit a true leader!

Can you hear those hushed whispers in the corners of the hall? Those are the ghosts of the Dead City, who have come to give their last tribute of respect to their lord! I don't know if he was a good king or a bad one, but he will have a truly royal death, hee hee! To fall by the hand of the great heroes of Sarnaut is a honorable end to any life. What's more, you can expect a truly royal reward, so get ready to fight. It will be a difficult fight!
It is not important how a person lived, all that is important is how they died.
The Dead King has finally found repose. The ancient tragedy has finally reached its proper end. And you receive the armor of the dead king as the victor.
Go the June Temple to the last ruin of the Chosen One and activate it.

Your Path is almost finished. It's time to start for June Temple, to the last June ruin and meet with the one we refer to as the "Mentor". He is a senior assistant to director in the Performance.
Keep in mind that only Ath-Zak's love, spiritual power, and perils through which he had been through, preserved the good name of the Junes throughout time. It wasn't the power of Tka-Rik no matter how great it is. One Chosen defeated one Curse. But a new Curse is of many faces - Astral has thousands and thousands of faces. It means that Chosen is to have many faces too.
Forget stupid fortune-telling and do what you have to do. And then with the help of Director we will prevent the June Executioner from destroying everything.

I had to break my mind into 12 pieces, 12 conditions of my mind, place them on the Chosen Path to let you through it and help to realize your role. It's pleasant to see you, to know that your spirit stood all the perils and finished the Path as I have predicted.
Before your last lesson I want to say something to you.
Those who you consider foes is the part of this world like you. You have done much evil to each other, but time is coming to forgive even the most horrible sins. Even Dragons call themselves Lords... Even madman wouldn't imagine that we would fight together. Believe me our enmity is older than League and Empire... But our unnatural alliance gives me hope. If we could have left past in the past, you can do it either. Just remember what we are fighting for.
Kill Rumbuckle Rebikov and give his belongings to Spirit of Wisdom.

Be ready to stand up for your Revelation, Chosen One. Your Way is almost finished, but the last step is always the most difficult one.
You may think the battle is easy, but to accept the truth that it brings will be much more difficult. Open your intelligence and don't be scared to believe in it regardless horrible it may seem.

I need Captain's belongings. Would you give them to me?
I want you to remember forever the sight of these two articles found together. A lot of evil could have been avoided if they had been found together many years ago...

Revelations of Tka-Rik and sign of cultist... Things speak for themselves.
"Revelations" that have triggered Great Astral Campaign and death of so many heroes, are fake. The captain you fought turned out to be a cultist, that's what his sign is saying.
Demons are not strangers from another world. No other worlds exist. No mysterious gates to be sealed up. Demons are one bone and one flesh of Sarnaut. But we will never manage to conclude a truce with them. They will never give up until they destroy us.
Return to Nezebgrad and tell Keeper of Secrets, Mark Staritsin, about your Revelation.

What do I do with this knowledge? Should I tell others? Those who laud the exploits of Skrakan and Nezeb? Those who will want to crucify you if you tell them they died for nothing?
No one will believe you. That's your personal Revelation. In time, others will experience it as well. That is when it will become the Truth.
But there's one person you need to tell this. Yasker? No. He already knows or suspects it.
Go to the Keeper of Secrets Mark Staritsin and tell him everything. It's his responsibility - learning secrets. Let him start a new chapter in the chronicle of the world. Let him touch the greatest secret.

I know everything!
You are not the first one to see! I'm flooded with messages that our history, everything we believed is fake!
Director of this crazy Play is very smart. Water wears away the stone! Yesterday I would rather laugh into your face having heard this news.
Today... Today I can only accept it with humility.
Let's wait. I'm sure this is not the last Revelation.
I'll soon be ready to call the spirit of the captain.
